title: Reversible Apply Planner with Economic Heuristics and State Reconciliation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Build a reversible config-apply planner that can (1) propose batching/caching configuration tweaks using cost heuristics, (2) apply them in a staged fashion with automated safety checks, and (3) reconcile state and perform safe automated rollbacks when preservation criteria or SLOs are violated. This ticket covers the planner, the trigger taxonomy, reconciliation loop, and the orchestration hooks for canary/staged applies. The system should operate with minimal human intervention for low-risk recommendations and require explicit approvals for high-risk changes.
acceptance_criteria: Planner can produce ranked change proposals for batching and prefix cache settings given workload profile input and historical cost data
Apply engine supports three modes: preview-only, staged-canary (traffic-split), and full-apply with automatic fallback
Trigger definitions include: SLO breach (p99 latency increase > 20% for 5m), error rate spike (>3x baseline for 3m), cost-per-token regression (>15% increase for 1h), and failed health checks
Rollback executes within 30s of trigger detection and confirms state reconciliation across controllers and the console UI
Audit trail records proposal, approval, diff, applied nodes, and rollback rationale in Drive/Confluence and emits corresponding event to observability pipeline
implementation_notes: Use existing config-change bus and add an "intent-id" to bind proposal <-> apply traces
Integrate cost model from Optimize service (read-only) to score proposals; fall back to default heuristics if service unavailable
Design reconciliation loop to compare desired config snapshot vs observed runtime state; use exponential backoff up to 5 retries before marking manual review required
Canary split implemented by traffic router tags: 'planner-canary-<intent-id>' and metric tags for per-intent SLOs
Keep change batches small: max 10% of pool or 2 nodes (whichever smaller) per step to minimize blast radius
Provide a safe-preview step that runs a dry-run and a simulated cost delta using the historical token distribution
risks_and_tradeoffs: Automated rollbacks can oscillate if triggers are too sensitive; we prefer conservative thresholds and hysteresis windows
Tighter batching reduces unit cost but can harm p99 latency; planner must surface latency vs cost trade-offs and allow operator override
Relying on Optimize service increases accuracy but adds a dependency; the planner must operate in graceful-degradation mode
Auditability and deterministic reconciliation logic are prioritized even if they add latency to the apply path
